title: Typewriter and Letter
premise: In the mountain town of Vellmark, apprentice clockmaker Ivo Ashgrove — a woman passing under her late brother's name — is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock, the mechanism by which the town's powerful Meridian Guild claims and distributes time itself. When the season's last bridge closes, Ivo discovers the clock's breakdown was no accident but sabotage by the Guild's dying patriarch, who means to bequeath his corrupt empire to whichever heir can 'hold time' longest. Hidden among the clockworks, Ivo finds letters proving the Guild's time records are fiction — and that her own brother died uncovering them. As the century turns, she must choose between restoring the lie that keeps Vellmark fed and letting the clock, and the Guild's power, stop forever; she finishes the work, but rewires it to ring true, and walks out over the spring bridge carrying her brother's name and her own at last.
about_author: Isandro Fairweather is the pen name of a former horologist's apprentice who spent a decade restoring municipal clocks across the northern ranges before turning to fiction. Their novels examine what towns keep running and what they quietly allow to stop.

chapters.title: The Summons in Winter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Summoned to the observatory as the first snows seal the passes, Ivo crosses the bridge with her tools and her brother's name stitched into her coat. The master clock is failing in ways no gear wear explains. She meets the Guild patriarch Aldous Meridian, who tests her with questions about silence and loyalty. Beat: wary belonging — she is needed, which is both shelter and trap.

chapters.title: Letters in the Works
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with interludes of her brother's letters found hidden in the clock's base. The bridge closes; the workshop becomes her whole world. Repairing the escapement, she uncovers her brother's correspondence proving the Guild's time records are fabricated to control wages and debts. Aldous's heirs circle, each more ruthless. Beat: rising dread — the silences she learned to keep now feel like complicity.

chapters.title: The Hour That Would Not Strike
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Aldous, dying, reveals he sabotaged the clock himself: a final test to choose an heir willing to preserve the lie. He offers Ivo the inheritance — legitimacy, protection, her brother's name made real — if she restores the clock as it was. The heirs discover the letters and hunt her through the observatory on the century's last night. Beat: climax — she chooses truth over belonging on the Guild's terms.

chapters.title: What the Bells Said
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, then the town's. At midnight she completes the repair — rewired to strike true — and the clock's honest hours begin undoing the Guild's debts as the old century dies. Aldous dies unthroned; the heirs scatter; the letters go public. Spring opens the bridge, and Ivo crosses it carrying both names. Beat: resolution — belonging rebuilt on truth, inheritance redefined as what we repair for others.
